newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary business says needs more active govt help.
newsitem.headline: Hungary business says needs more active govt help.

text.p: Hungary's major industrialists on Monday accused the government of reneging on commitments to help private enterprise and called for lower taxes and national action for key sectors.

"The government says it supports us in principle but concrete steps are yet to be taken," Gabor Szeles, president of the Hungarian Industrialists' Association (GYOSZ), which represents 80 percent of the country's industrial base, told a news conference.
Speaking after the organisation's annual general meeting, Szeles said Hungary needs national programmes to help four main sectors -- the vehicle industry, electronics, energy and retail.
Szeles said domestic consumption was an important element of sustainable growth, which cannot be achieved only by promoting exports. The domestic market accounts for 64 percent of GDP, he said.
He also complained about "brutally high taxes", especially local authority tax, which is based on company output.
"It is a dark medieval concept to have local taxes as a percentage of turnover," he said.
Szeles expressed concern at the current mushrooming multi-million-dollar western-style shopping centres such as the recently opened Duna Plaza and Polus malls in Budapest.
He called for the government to focus some of its attention on solving the conflict between small retailers and the new malls.
"(GYOSZ) fully supports shopping malls, but the interests of small retaliers also have to be considered," he said.
Prime Minister Gyula Horn was supposed to be the guest of honour of the general meeting but instead sent a letter assuring GYOSZ of his full support.
